subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: A cross section is the two-dimensional figure you get when a flat plane slices through a three-dimensional solid. The shape of the cross section depends on the solid and on how the slicing plane is oriented. In this worksheet you will identify, name, and measure cross sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $6$ cm long, $4$ cm wide, and $3$ cm tall. A plane slices the prism parallel to its top and bottom faces. Name the two-dimensional cross section and give its dimensions.
items.answer: A rectangle that is $6$ cm by $4$ cm

steps: A slice parallel to a face of a rectangular prism produces a cross section congruent to that face.
The top and bottom faces are the length-by-width faces, which are $6$ cm by $4$ cm.
So the cross section is a rectangle measuring $6$ cm by $4$ cm.

items.prompt: A cube has edges of length $5$ in. A plane slices the cube parallel to one of its faces. Name the cross section and give its dimensions.
items.answer: A square that is $5$ in by $5$ in

steps: Every face of a cube is a square with side equal to the edge length, $5$ in.
A slice parallel to a face is congruent to that face.
So the cross section is a $5$ in by $5$ in square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $8$ m by $8$ m by $2$ m. A plane slices it parallel to a $8$ m by $8$ m face. Name the cross section and give its dimensions.
items.answer: A square that is $8$ m by $8$ m

steps: A slice parallel to a face matches that face exactly.
The chosen face is $8$ m by $8$ m, and since both dimensions are equal it is a square.
So the cross section is a $8$ m by $8$ m square.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a rectangular base that is $10$ ft by $6$ ft. A plane slices the pyramid parallel to the base, partway up toward the apex. What is the shape of the cross section?
items.answer: A rectangle (a smaller rectangle similar to the base)

steps: A slice of a pyramid parallel to its base has the same shape as the base.
The base here is a rectangle, so the cross section is a rectangle.
It is a smaller rectangle similar to the $10$ ft by $6$ ft base, not a triangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $7$ cm by $4$ cm by $4$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face. What is the area of the cross section?

steps: The slice is parallel to the $7$ cm by $4$ cm face, so the cross section is a $7$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle.
Area of a rectangle is length times width: $7 \times 4 = 28$.
So the cross-section area is $28 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $8$ in long, $5$ in wide, and $2$ in tall. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the length, slicing through the $5$ in by $2$ in face. Name the cross section and give its dimensions.
items.answer: A rectangle that is $5$ in by $2$ in

steps: Cutting perpendicular to the length exposes the width and the height of the prism, not the length.
The width is $5$ in and the height is $2$ in.
So the cross section is a rectangle measuring $5$ in by $2$ in.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $9$ cm long, $9$ cm wide, and $4$ cm tall. A vertical plane cuts straight down, perpendicular to the width. Name the cross section, give its dimensions, and find its area.
items.answer: A rectangle $9$ cm by $4$ cm with area $36 \text{ cm}^2$

steps: Cutting perpendicular to the width exposes the length and the height.
The length is $9$ cm and the height is $4$ cm, so the cross section is a $9$ cm by $4$ cm rectangle.
Its area is $9 \times 4 = 36 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid is sliced by a vertical plane that passes through the apex and runs parallel to a pair of base edges. What two-dimensional figure is the cross section?

steps: A plane through the apex of a pyramid contains the single top point and a segment across the base.
It meets two lateral faces and the base, giving three sides that meet at the apex.
A three-sided figure is a triangle, so the cross section is a triangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism measures $12$ mm by $7$ mm by $7$ mm. A plane slices it parallel to a $7$ mm by $7$ mm face. Name the cross section and find its area.
items.answer: A square $7$ mm by $7$ mm with area $49 \text{ mm}^2$

steps: The slice is parallel to a $7$ mm by $7$ mm face, so the cross section matches that face.
Because both dimensions are $7$ mm, the cross section is a square.
Its area is $7 \times 7 = 49 \text{ mm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a vertical plane that passes through its apex and is parallel to one pair of base edges. The base measures $12$ cm in that direction and the pyramid is $9$ cm tall. The slice forms a triangle whose base is the full $12$ cm and whose height is the pyramid's height. Find the area of this triangular cross section.

steps: The cross section through the apex is a triangle with base $12$ cm and height $9$ cm.
Area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
$\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 9 = \frac{1}{2} \times 108 = 54$.
So the cross-section area is $54 \text{ cm}^2$.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $10$ ft by $6$ ft and a height of $8$ ft. A plane slices it parallel to the base, halfway up the height. Name the cross section and give its exact dimensions.
items.answer: A rectangle that is $5$ ft by $3$ ft

steps: A slice parallel to the base is similar to the base, so it is a rectangle.
At a fraction $\frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}$ of the way down from the apex, the linear dimensions scale by $\frac{1}{2}$. (Halfway up the height is halfway down from the apex.)
Length: $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 = 5$ ft. Width: $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 = 3$ ft.
So the cross section is a $5$ ft by $3$ ft rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid has a base $12$ cm by $9$ cm and a height of $12$ cm. A plane slices it parallel to the base at a height of $8$ cm above the base (so $4$ cm below the apex). Find the dimensions of the rectangular cross section.
items.answer: A rectangle that is $4$ cm by $3$ cm

steps: The cross section is similar to the base, scaled by the ratio of its distance below the apex to the full height.
The slice is $12 - 8 = 4$ cm below the apex, and the full height is $12$ cm, so the scale factor is $\frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}$.
Length: $\frac{1}{3} \times 12 = 4$ cm. Width: $\frac{1}{3} \times 9 = 3$ cm.
So the cross section is a $4$ cm by $3$ cm rectangle.

items.prompt: A right rectangular pyramid is cut by a plane that is parallel to one pair of opposite base edges but tilted (not parallel to the base) and not passing through the apex, intersecting all four lateral faces. Name the resulting cross section and explain why it has that shape.
items.answer: A trapezoid (a quadrilateral with the top edge shorter than the bottom edge)

steps: The plane crosses all four lateral faces, so the cross section is a four-sided figure (a quadrilateral).
Because the plane is parallel to one pair of opposite base edges, the two cuts across the faces containing those edges are parallel to each other.
The pyramid narrows toward the apex, so the higher of those two parallel cuts is shorter than the lower one.
One pair of parallel sides of unequal length means the figure is a trapezoid. It is not a rectangle (the parallel sides differ in length) and not a triangle (it has four sides).

items.prompt: A right rectangular prism is $6$ cm by $6$ cm by $6$ cm (a cube). A plane slices straight down diagonally through two opposite vertical edges, so the cut goes from one vertical edge to the diagonally opposite vertical edge. The cross section is a rectangle whose height is the cube's height and whose width is the diagonal of the $6$ cm by $6$ cm top face. Find the exact dimensions of the cross section.

steps: The diagonal slice goes between opposite vertical edges, so one side of the cross section is the diagonal of the square top face.
The top face is $6$ cm by $6$ cm, so its diagonal is $\sqrt{6^2 + 6^2} = \sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}$ cm.
The other side of the cross section is the vertical height of the cube, $6$ cm.
So the cross section is a rectangle measuring $6\sqrt{2}$ cm by $6$ cm.

items.prompt: A triangular pyramid (a tetrahedron) has $4$ triangular faces. A student claims that slicing it with a single flat plane can produce a pentagon (a five-sided figure). Is this possible? Explain your reasoning using the number of faces a plane can cross.
items.answer: No, it is not possible; the tetrahedron has only $4$ faces, so a single plane crosses at most $4$ of them and the cross section has at most $4$ sides.

steps: A triangular pyramid (tetrahedron) has exactly $4$ faces.
When a single flat plane slices a solid, it contributes at most one straight edge of the cross section for each face it passes through.
With only $4$ faces available, the plane can create at most $4$ edges, so the cross section has at most $4$ sides.

A pentagon has $5$ sides, which would require crossing $5$ faces. Since the tetrahedron has only $4$ faces, a pentagon cross section is impossible. (The most you can get is a triangle or a quadrilateral.)
